en: The Theravāda Vinaya:
Bhikkhunīvibhaṅga,
Pācittiyakaṇḍa
The Chapter on Tuvaṭṭa 40.
The Training Rule on Setting Out on a Wander.
At that time, the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Rājagaha in the Bamboo Grove, the Squirrels’ Feeding Place.
Now at that time, the bhikkhunīs were spending the rains retreat right there in Rājagaha, the winter there, and the summer there.
People complained, grumbled, and spread it about, saying:
"The quarters for the bhikkhunīs are crowded and dark; these quarters do not open out onto the open air."
The bhikkhunīs heard those people grumbling, complaining, and expressing their indignation.
Then those bhikkhunīs informed the bhikkhus of this matter.
The bhikkhus informed the Blessed One of this matter.
Then the Blessed One, having given a discourse on the Dhamma with reference to this cause and this occasion, addressed the bhikkhus:
“In that case, bhikkhus, I will lay down a training rule for the bhikkhunīs, based on ten reasons:
for the well-being of the Saṅgha … [and so forth] …”
For the endurance of the true Dhamma and for the support of the Vinaya.
And thus, monks, should the nuns recite this training rule:
"Whichever nun, having completed the rains residence, does not set out on a journey, even if it be only five or six yojanas, incurs an offense of expiation."
"But whichever" means whichever such... "nun" means...
[as before]... nun.
...pe... this is the nun intended in this context.
One who has completed the rains residence means one who has completed either the first three months or the last three months.
“I will not set out on a journey, even for as little as five or six yojanas”— if one merely abandons the burden [of the journey], there is an offense of *pācittiya*.
There is no offense if there is an obstacle.
If she has searched for a companion nun but does not find one,
or if she is ill,
or in times of distress.
"In the case of one who is insane,
or for one who is a first-time offender.
The tenth training rule is concluded.
The fourth chapter, on Tuvaṭṭa, is concluded.
